title: Reading for Meaning
keyIdea: Reading is not just saying the words. Reading means you get what the words mean. As you read, ask: does it make sense? Can I see a picture of it in my head? If it sounds silly, stop and read it again. When you finish, try to tell it back.

kid: Bip the robot can say every word. But Bip does not know what the words mean. So Bip is not really reading. Reading means you get it.
As you read, ask: does it make sense? "We swam in the cake" is silly. You can't swim in a cake! A word was read wrong. It should say lake.
If it does not make sense, stop. Go back and read it again. Look at each word. Small words like on and under matter too.
Make a picture in your head as you read. When you get to the end, tell it back. What came first, next and last? If you can tell it, you got it.
adult: This topic is for ages 5 to 6. It is the idea behind all reading: the goal is meaning, not just turning letters into sounds. A child who reads every word aloud but cannot say what happened has decoded the text without reading it. Researchers describe reading as decoding times language comprehension; both are needed, and if either is zero, reading is zero.

The habit to build is self-monitoring: asking "Does that make sense?" while reading. Children who monitor notice when a misread word turns a sentence into nonsense, then stop, reread and fix it. Praise the self-correction itself, as well as the right word. Visualising the scene and retelling the story in order are two simple ways to check that the meaning got through.

Common mistakes: reading fast and smoothly with no idea what happened; reading on past a sentence that makes no sense; swapping in a word that looks similar (goat for coat) and not noticing; skipping small words like on, in and under; and retelling events out of order. Be careful not to jump in at once with the right word. Wait a moment, then ask "Does that make sense?" so your child learns to check.

In the lab your child hears Bip the robot read a sentence perfectly but fail to say what it means, picks the matching picture, decides whether four sentences make sense, finds and fixes a misread word, drags things to where the words say, and retells a short story in order.

familyTip: When your child misreads a word, pause and ask "Does that make sense?" instead of correcting straight away. After a page, ask them to tell you what happened, or to point at the part of the picture the words describe.

practice.prompt: Bip reads "The pig is in the mud" with no mistakes. Bip can't say where the pig is. Did Bip really read it?
choices: No, Bip did not get the meaning
practice.hint: Reading means more than saying the words. What else do you need?
practice.explain: Bip said every word right, but did not get what it means. Reading means you get the meaning.

practice.prompt: Ella reads: "I ate {n} grapes for my snake." Does it make sense?
practice.hint: Do you eat grapes for a snake? Which word looks like snake?
practice.explain: You eat grapes for a snack, not a snake. Snake and snack look alike, so Ella should stop and read it again.

practice.prompt: You read a sentence and it sounds silly. What should you do?
practice.hint: If it is silly, maybe a word was read wrong.
practice.explain: Stop and go back. Read each word again so the sentence makes sense.

practice.prompt: "The {n} ducks swim under the bridge." Where are the ducks?
choices: Below the bridge, in the water
practice.hint: Under is a small word. What does it tell you?
practice.explain: Under means below. The ducks swim in the water below the bridge.

practice.prompt: "Sam fell off his bike. Mum put a plaster on his knee." What happened first?
practice.hint: Tell it back. What happened before Mum helped?
practice.explain: First Sam fell off. Next Mum put a plaster on his knee. Telling it in order shows you got it.

pool.hint: Bip says the words. What does Bip miss?
pool.explain: Reading means you get the meaning. Saying the words is only part of it.

pool.prompt: Leo reads: "Put on your goat, it is cold." Which word makes sense?
pool.hint: What do you put on when it is cold?
pool.explain: You put on a coat when it is cold. Goat looks a bit like coat, but it does not make sense.

pool.prompt: "The cat is on the box." Where is the cat?
pool.hint: On is a small word. What does it tell you?
pool.explain: On means on top. Small words like on, in and under change the picture.

pool.prompt: Zoe reads "The sun is cold and wet." What should she think?
choices: That is silly, I will read it again
pool.hint: Is the sun cold and wet? Does it make sense?
pool.explain: The sun is hot and dry, so it does not make sense. A word may be read wrong. She should read it again.

pool.prompt: "Tom has {n} red balloons." Which picture fits?
pool.hint: Check each word: how many, and what colour?
pool.explain: The words say {n} and red. A picture that fits shows every part of the sentence.

pool.prompt: "Mia planted {n} seeds. She gave them water. Flowers grew!" What happened last?
pool.hint: Tell it in order: first, next, last.
pool.explain: First Mia planted {n} seeds, next she gave them water, and last the flowers grew.

pool.prompt: How can you check you got the meaning?
choices: Tell it back in your own words
pool.hint: What can you do when you get to the end?
pool.explain: If you can tell it back, you got it. Counting words does not show the meaning.

pool.prompt: "The fish ___ in the pond." Which word makes it make sense?
pool.hint: What does a fish do in a pond?
pool.explain: A fish swims in a pond. Reading means checking the words make sense together.

pool.prompt: Dad reads "The dog sat on the log" as "The dog sat on the dog." What went wrong?
choices: One word was read wrong, so it is silly
pool.hint: Can a dog sit on a dog? Look at the last word.
pool.explain: A dog cannot sit on itself, so it is silly. Log and dog look alike. Reading the last word again fixes it.

visual.caption: Read each sentence. Does it make sense, or is it silly? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: The cat sat on the mat.
I rode my bike to the bark.
The sun is cold and wet.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: Bip says words but misses the meaning; pick the picture, spot silly sentences, fix a misread word, place things, retell.
